title: Finite affine module charts for eventual flatness descent
statement: Let $I$ be a directed partially ordered set, $R:I\to\mathrm{CommRing}$ a ring diagram, $c$ a limiting cone of $\operatorname{Spec}(R_k)$ with affine point, $i\in I$, and $f:X_i\to\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)$ a finitely presented morphism [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-morphism-conventions]. Let $M$ be a finitely presented quasi-coherent module on $X_i$. Suppose its pullback to $X_i\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)}c.\mathrm{pt}$ is flat over $c.\mathrm{pt}$ [def-pc-base-change] [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Put $C=\operatorname{colim}R$, with the specified coprojection $R_i\to C$. There exist $n\in\mathbb N$, commutative rings $B_b$, $B_b$-modules $N_b$, and ring maps $a_b:R_i\to B_b$, for $b\in\operatorname{Fin}(n)$, such that $B_b$ is finitely presented over $R_i$ and $N_b$ is finitely presented over $B_b$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. For a coprojection or transition $R_i\to T$, put $D_T=T\otimes_{R_i}R_i$ with its right $R_i$-algebra structure, and restrict $N_b$ along $a_b$. Each $D_C\otimes_{R_i}N_b$ is flat over $D_C$. For every $k\ge i$, if every $D_{R_k}\otimes_{R_i}N_b$ is flat over $D_{R_k}$, then the pullback of $M$ to $X_i\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)}\operatorname{Spec}(R_k)$ is flat over $\operatorname{Spec}(R_k)$. This is finite affine comparison and gluing, with no assertion of eventual flatness.

proof.text: Because Spec(R_i) is quasi-compact and f is quasi-compact, X_i is quasi-compact. Choose a finite affine open cover U_b, b in Fin(n), using [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover]. Set B_b = Gamma(U_b,O_X), N_b = Gamma(U_b,M), and let a_b be f on sections, composed with the canonical R_i-isomorphism for global sections of Spec(R_i). Local finite presentation makes B_b a finitely presented R_i-algebra by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation]. The modules N_b are finitely presented over B_b by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-affine-sections]. These are actual section rings and modules, not data chosen in definitions from a holed existence statement.

proof.text: Let C be the point of the chosen colimit cocone of R. The affine-limit comparison [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition-affine-comparison], together with the natural isomorphisms Gamma(Spec(R_k)) = R_k, identifies c.pt with Spec(C). The uniqueness equations for a colimit identify its coprojections with the ring maps corresponding to the cone projections. For any later k, and for C, the inverse images of U_b are spectra of T tensor_{R_i} B_b by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. The affine pullback sections theorem [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] identifies the pulled-back module with T tensor_{R_i} N_b, with the base-ring action induced by the second pullback projection.

source.place: Lemma 32.10.4, Tag 05LY, finite affine reduction, specialized to Y_i = S_i; Properties Tag 01PC; Morphisms Tag 01U4

proof.text: For T = C and for T = R_k, put D_T = T tensor_{R_i} R_i. The maps t tensor r to t*a(r), and t to t tensor 1, are inverse ring isomorphisms D_T = T; the tensor balancing relations show that their composites are identity. After restricting N_b along a_b, the induced tensor module D_T tensor_{R_i} N_b is canonically T tensor_{R_i} N_b, with all scalar actions respected. Transport limit flatness on each chart across these isomorphisms to obtain the displayed flat limit module.

source.place: Tag 01U4, affine-section characterization (1) implies (2), with tensor-unit identifications

proof.text: At any stage k, flatness of the displayed D_{R_k}-modules transports to flatness of the chart sections over R_k. For every point of a chart, localization preserves flatness over the localized base ring. Since the pulled-back affine charts cover the stage source, all relative module stalks are flat. For an arbitrary affine source test open over an affine base test open, quasi-coherence identifies its localized section modules with these stalks. The prime-local criterion [lem-pc-affine-sections-flat-over-base] then makes its section module flat over the base test ring, which is precisely [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. This proves the stage implication, without applying any eventual descent theorem. If X_i is empty choose n=0; every source base change is empty and its sections are zero modules. Zero rings and zero modules satisfy the same comparison formulas.
